author: NorthEast News Desk
body: At least 24 children were killed when a fire tore through two schools and about 300 wooden homes in Bukavu, a city in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo controlled by AFC/M23 rebels, a local official said Thursday.

The dead included 19 girls and five boys, according to South Kivu’s vice governor in the rebel-appointed administration. Twenty-nine people were reported injured, although accounts from hospitals and residents indicated that the toll could change as officials reconcile casualties.
The fire was out by Thursday afternoon, but smoke continued to rise from rubble and twisted roofing, a Reuters witness reported. Investigators had not determined the cause.

Bukavu has been under the control of the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 movement since its rapid advance through eastern Congo in 2025. That conflict complicates public administration and emergency response in a densely populated city. The immediate priorities are identifying victims, treating the injured, sheltering families whose homes were destroyed and establishing how flames spread into school buildings. Officials and health workers cautioned that the death toll could rise, making this an active emergency with significant uncertainty around the final number of victims.
dek: Officials said 19 girls and five boys were among the dead as flames also destroyed roughly 300 wooden homes in the rebel-held city.
headline: Bukavu fire kills at least 24 children and destroys two schools
